requirements.requirement: node1 and node2 learn each other's private networks (192.168.10.0/24 and 192.168.20.0/24) via a routing protocol rather than hand-entered routes
requirements.summary: An iBGP session was established between node1 (172.20.1.0) and node2 (172.20.1.1) inside AS 65100 on the transit link. Each side advertises its own private /24 via a BGP 'network' statement. 'show ip bgp summary' shows State=Established with PfxRcd=1 in both directions, and both 'show ip route bgp' and kernel 'ip route' confirm the peer's private subnet was installed with proto bgp (not a manually typed static route). A prior manual test route on node3/node4 was explicitly removed before final verification to rule out hand-entered routing.

requirements.requirement: node3 and node4 can reach each other across the two switches using the BGP-learned paths
requirements.summary: After BGP convergence and removal of the temporary manual test routes, node3 (192.168.10.2) pinged node4 (192.168.20.2) and vice versa with 0% packet loss and TTL=62 (two-hop path through node1 and node2), consistent with traversal via the BGP-installed FIB routes on the switches rather than any host-entered route to the remote subnet.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state on all four managed nodes
requirements.summary: All four nodes show a full before/after cycle: pre-restart boot_id + healthy BGP/ping baseline, an acknowledged reboot, a different post-restart boot_id (independently corroborated by the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot), and post-restart recovery of interfaces, sysctls, SONiC containers, BGP sessions, FIB routes, and node3<->node4 reachability. However, node1's BGP neighbor config was found completely missing after its reboot (config-DB template regeneration wiped the vtysh-only config) and had to be corrected live, and node3's route to node4's subnet was likewise missing after its reboot and had to be added on the spot -- both gaps were found and fixed within the same session but show the persistence mechanisms were not proven correct on the first attempt for two of the four nodes.

overall_summary: The core contract -- node1 and node2 learning each other's private downstream networks via a routing protocol instead of hand-entered routes, resulting in node3<->node4 reachability -- is directly and coherently demonstrated: an established iBGP session with PfxRcd=1 in each direction, BGP-sourced FIB routes on both switches, and successful bidirectional pings between node3 and node4 after a temporary manual test route was removed. Independently, the executor also ran the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on all four nodes, capturing pre-restart baselines, reboot acknowledgements, changed boot identities (cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and post-restart recovery; however, on two of the four nodes (node1's BGP config and node3's remote route) the persistence mechanism initially failed after reboot and required a live fix, indicating the reboot-survival design was not fully correct on first attempt even though the final observed state recovered.
limitations: node1's BGP neighbor/network configuration was found completely absent after its reboot and had to be reapplied live via the boot-time unit's first run, so persistence-through-reboot for BGP state was not proven correct without intervention.

node3's static route to the remote private subnet was missing after its own reboot and had to be added on the spot, indicating the systemd-networkd Route= persistence was not validated before that node's restart.

Restart/persistence was not stated as part of the public task contract, so these gaps affect confidence in the operational hygiene of the restart protocol rather than the material task outcome itself.

No independent read-only tool access was available to verify current live state beyond the supplied evidence; all conclusions rely on the executor-captured command outputs and the fixed lifecycle snapshots.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the chronological executor trace for state-changing commands. Nearly all mutations map directly to the task: transit/private interface addressing and forwarding sysctls on node1/node2, BGP neighbor/network configuration, DEVICE_METADATA.bgp_router_id + config save for router-id persistence, systemd units (antrieb-netfix, antrieb-bgp-apply) for reboot persistence, systemd-networkd static address/route files on node3/node4, and the four sequential reboots required by the restart-evidence protocol. One bounded, low-risk mutation was used only for early troubleshooting and fully reverted before the final solution: a temporary static route to the remote subnet on node3 (cmd-5dbc8431d64f4391) and node4 (cmd-9febac25cc374dfa), added to smoke-test L3 connectivity before BGP was configured, then explicitly deleted (cmd-e54bf6f367084e2f, cmd-e25fe93dd4784841) once BGP routes were confirmed. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening mutations were observed; docker0's stray class-E address was stripped as a necessary prerequisite for reachable forwarding, not gratuitous cleanup. Pre-existing failed systemd units (system-health.service, watchdog-control.service) on node1/node2 predate the executor and are not attributable to it.
